source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. CPU Common Options → SMU and PSP Debug Mode: Disabled e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Uncorrectable Error Injection sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --smupsp --socket 0 --errormode 2 --ccd 0 --enablemcapolling 0 --errorindex 0 --errortype 1 5.1 The system will reset immediately. 5.2 When system boot into operating system again, check dmesg log. 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. For uncorrectable errors, verify that the errors are logged correctly in BERT dmesg after the warm reset is triggered. 3. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 4. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- MP5 Uncorrectable Error: inject the MP5 MP5 Uncorrectable Error via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'smu|mp1|mp5|mpio|firmware.error|corrected|uncorrected'; echo __MP5_MP5_Uncorrectable_Error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

test_case.purpose: Inject an MP5 uncorrectable error at the intended socket/CCD/index, verify immediate warm reset and a fresh MP5-attributed persistent record, then prove the target CCD and firmware-managed services recover after boot.
required_package: Vendor semantics for errormode2, CCD0, mcapolling0 and errortype1
FFE threshold, debug-disable and SyncFlood relevance plus raw restoration values
Fresh MP5-specific MCA/BERT/CPER/WHEA/SEL and reset-cause fields
Reset, firmware, boot and OS-report deadlines
CCD compute, memory and SMU sensor/power/thermal recovery limits, aborts and OOB restoration
test_case.test_command: Approve the MP5-to-CCD map and full tuple; baseline reset/BERT and controller state; inject once under OOB console; capture reset/firmware/boot intervals; decode fresh MP5 UCE evidence; verify cores, NUMA, memory, sensors and power/thermal controls; restore thresholds, debug settings and HDT state.

If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
